name: Prior period items
definition: Prior period items are income or expenses that arise in the current period as a result of ERRORS OR OMISSIONS in the preparation of the financial statements of one or more prior periods. Their nature and amount must be separately disclosed in the statement of profit and loss so their impact on the current profit or loss can be perceived. They are normally included in determining the current period's net profit or loss.
why_it_exists: It separates 'the earlier statements were wrong' from 'circumstances changed'. Only the first is a prior period item. For a system that posts corrections, this is the deciding question: an error correction carries a separate-disclosure obligation, and a change in circumstances does not.
inputs: the income or expense arising in the current period
the cause: an error or omission in preparing a prior period's financial statements, or something else
the prior period or periods affected
outputs: classification as a prior period item, separately disclosed
or a determination that it is NOT a prior period item
preconditions: an item of income or expense has arisen in the current period
its cause can be traced to the preparation of one or more prior periods' financial statements
exceptions: other adjustments necessitated by circumstances which, though related to prior periods, are determined in the current period, are NOT prior period items
income or expense recognised on the outcome of a contingency that previously could not be estimated reliably is NOT a prior period item
common_mistakes: treating any adjustment that touches a prior period as a prior period item — AS 5 paragraph 16 restricts the term to errors and omissions only
classifying retrospective wage arrears as a prior period item, which AS 5 paragraph 16 names as the counterexample
classifying a revised estimate as a prior period item, which AS 5 paragraph 21 explicitly excludes
burying the correction inside the ordinary line item instead of disclosing its nature and amount separately
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing not extracted; only ICAI AS-1 and AS-5 were read for this claim, so no statute is cited
icai_references: AS 5, paragraph 4, definition of prior period items
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — AS-1 and AS-5 govern financial-statement policy and period attribution; GST is a separate determination and must not be conflated with it
evidence_required: identification of the prior period whose financial statements contained the error or omission
the nature of the error: a mathematical mistake, a mistake in applying an accounting policy, a misinterpretation of facts, or an oversight
the amount of the income or expense arising in the current period
confidence_factors: weak when it cannot be established whether the prior statements were wrong, or merely based on what was known at the time
strong when the cause is a mathematical mistake, which is checkable by recomputation rather than by judgement
weak when a later payment could be either a correction of an omission or a new obligation created retrospectively — AS 5 paragraph 16 treats the wage-arrears form of that as NOT a prior period item
validation_checks: the cause is an error or omission in preparing a prior period's financial statements, not a change in circumstances determined in the current period
the item is not a revision of an accounting estimate
the nature and the amount are separately disclosed so their impact on the current profit or loss can be perceived
the item is included in determining the current period's net profit or loss, or shown after that determination — either way its effect on current profit or loss is indicated
examples: an expense omitted from last year's statements by oversight, discovered and recognised this year — a prior period item, separately disclosed
counterexamples: arrears payable to workers as a result of a retrospective wage revision during the current period — AS 5 paragraph 16 states this is NOT a prior period item, though it relates to prior periods
income recognised on the outcome of a contingency that previously could not be estimated reliably — AS 5 paragraph 18 states this does not constitute a prior period item

evidence.quote: Prior period items are generally infrequent in nature and can be distinguished from changes in accounting estimates. Accounting estimates by their nature are approximations that may need revision as additional information becomes known. For example, income or expense recognised on the outcome of a contingency which previously could not be estimated reliably does not constitute a prior period item.

Prior period items are normally included in the determination of net profit or loss for the current period. An alternative approach is to show such items in the statement of profit and loss after determination of current net profit or loss. In either case, the objective is to indicate the effect of such items on the current profit or loss.
